# Phone-only supplemental hosts entries, appended to the canonical hosts file
# generated by ~/hosts-blocker during deploy staging.
#
# Why here and not in hosts-blocker: that generator is shared with the PC,
# where these entries would be dead weight. This file is the phone's own
# layer, which is what "all phone changes in one repo" means. It follows the
# same precedent as strip_workout_hosts.py, which already post-processes the
# generated canonical for phone-specific reasons.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE PLAY STORE IS NOT BLOCKED HERE, AND MUST NOT BE. Read this before adding
# a play/finsky/gstatic hostname.
#
# Play is GEOFENCED, not blocked: the enforcer hides com.android.vending at
# home (day and night) and shows it again on the AWAY branch. See
# docs/DOCS-policy-lists.md#why-the-play-store-is-blocked-at-home-only
#
# A hosts file cannot express that. It is one static file, identical at home
# and away, so any Play hostname listed here would apply on the AWAY branch
# too -- exactly where the policy deliberately makes Play work.
#
# And it would not merely make Play slow. Measured on device 2026-08-24:
# infakt is wrapped in Google PairIP license verification and performs a
# license check against Play on startup. Break that and infakt shows
# "Something went wrong / Check that Google Play is enabled" and refuses to
# open at all -- the precise failure this whole policy is built to avoid.
# android.clients.google.com is the classic licensing/checkin endpoint, so it
# is the most tempting and the most damaging entry to add.
#
# DO NOT ADD, under any circumstances:
#   android.clients.google.com   - Play licensing / device checkin
#   play.googleapis.com          - Play backend
#   mtalk.google.com             - the FCM persistent connection
#   fcm.googleapis.com           - FCM send/registration
#   android.googleapis.com       - GMS checkin/registration
#   *.googleapis.com wholesale
#
# The app layer is what blocks Play, and it is the correct layer: hiding the
# package is geofence-aware, and a hidden package cannot be launched at all.
# This file exists as the phone's hook for future phone-only host blocks; it
# deliberately blocks nothing today rather than being deleted, because the
# deploy staging path and its guard tests are worth keeping wired up.
